scope: Read-only live timing probes of the existing embedded Linear MCP bridge. No production edits. No model turns. Existing Codex OAuth and workspace verification preserved.
current_code_findings: WithReviewLinks has a shared eight-second budget and resolves unique cache misses sequentially.
Each NativeReviewClient.Resolve starts Node, discovers Codex configuration, starts a Codex app-server, creates an ephemeral thread, verifies the workspace, calls get_diff and shuts down.
The previous change deduplicates duplicate PR URLs within a repository/account scope, but distinct PRs still repeat connection setup.
Successful Linear review links have a five-minute cache; confirmed missing reviews have a one-minute cache. Transient failures are not cached as missing.
recommended_strategy: Add a batched review provider method behind MetadataService; commands and later Lua bindings keep the same metadata request.
Resolve connection selection per repository first; reuse a session only when selected account/profile/configuration match. Cache keys remain scoped per repository and account configuration.
Verify workspace once per session before any review lookup; retain exact PR URL and Linear review workspace validation per result.
Start with sequential requests through one reused session, then measure a small bounded concurrency if needed.
Publish GitHub PR/CI observations independently of optional Linear enrichment so a slow review lookup cannot delay all visible metadata.
Keep successful/missing review caches and deduplicate pending work. Preserve cancellation, unavailable-vs-missing semantics and GitHub fallback.
Treat rate-limit responses explicitly and honor provider backoff; do not assume GitHub concurrency limits apply to Linear MCP.
Consider direct Linear GraphQL only after supported authentication and review/diff schema are verified; do not extract or repurpose Codex MCP OAuth credentials.
limitations: One single-PR probe and one three-PR reused-session probe; no sustained-load or large-batch validation.
Measured phase totals exclude binary lookup, some local parsing and process cleanup. These are not full CLI wall-clock times.
One verified Alita account was used deliberately across three repository URLs. Automatic multi-repository connection grouping is not implemented or validated.
Linear public GraphQL rate limits do not establish the rate limits of the MCP transport.
Targeted GitHub GraphQL remains a separate prototype; the production metadata API still uses the old GitHub transport.
